 Judgment
1.
This case has arisen out of accident which occurred on 10.08.2016 at about 07:45 pm.
Deceased was coming to home RAKESH from Priya Chowk Railway Road with her son Sonbir.

When she KUMAR SINGH reached at NH-58, near Chauki Railway Road, in front of RAKESH KUMAR Ukhlarsi, a truck bearing No.UP-11T-4219 which was coming from the side of Meerut and going towards Gaziabad came at a very high speed and rashly/negligently driven by its driver.
The accident resulted into death of deceased Maya Devi.
The police registered an FIR No.623/2016 and investigated the matter.
The legal-heirs of Maya Devi has filed claim petition for the purpose of compensation.
2. The Ld. Predecessor conducted the proceedings.
The driver and owner appeared and filed joint reply admitting that the accident took place on 10.08.2016 on NH 58.

They submitted that at the time of accident the driver of truck bearing No. UP 11T/4219 was driving the truck very carefully,
with in the speed limits following the traffic rules and regulations.
The insurance company also filed reply.

On the basis of available material, the Ld. Predecessor framed following issues:
1. Whether Maya Devi sustained fatal injuries in a motor vehicle accident dt.
10.8.2016 due to rash or negligent driving of vehicle no. UP-11T-4219 being driven by respondent no. 1 Man Singh, owned by respondent no. 2 Krashak Motor Parivahan Sahkari Samiti Ltd. and insured by respondent no. 3 National Insurance Co. Ltd?
...

sentences.text: OPP 2.

Whther the petititioner is entititled to claim Digitally signed by RAKESH compensation, if so,
what amount and from RAKESH KUMAR KUMAR SINGH whom? ...
Relief.
3. During the evidence, the petitioner Sh. Sonbir examined himself by way of affidavit and was cross examined on behalf of respondents.
The respondent no. 3 examined one Sh. Surjeet Singh, Assistant of National Insurance Co. Ltd and one Sh. Sunil Giriwal, Assistant with complete record of DL No.UP-12 19860002289.
They were cross examined and thereafter RE was closed.
Both the sides have been heard.
This judgment will disposed off the case.
4. Occurrence of accident has been mentioned in the FIR and charge-sheet.
Involvement of the offending vehicle is also mentioned so.
In terms of Rule 7 of Delhi Motor Accidents Claims Tribunals Rules 2008, the FIR and charge-sheet have to be accepted for their contents.

entities.text: Delhi Motor Accidents Claims Tribunals Rules 2008
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 5. The driver has claimed that he was driving in proper manner.
This claim itself shows that the offending vehicle was present at the spot.
Once, the charge-sheet has found the driver as culprit, a prima-facie presumption can be taken that offending driver was rash/negligent.

It was then for the Meena Devi vs Man Singh And Ors on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145693799/
2 driver to dispute the rashness/ negligence.

entities.text: Meena Devi vs Man Singh And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The driver/owner have not led any evidence to support the proper driving.
Once this is so, there is no reason as to why the contents of charge-sheet should not be RAKESH KUMAR accepted.

If the insurance company was of the view that deceased SINGH was solely negligent, it should have appointed its own investigator to investigate the accident and should have led 17:59:15 +0530 evidence in support of its claim.
The insurance company has done neither.
It is clear that accident happened due to rash/ negligent driving of Man Singh.
Issue No. 1 is decided in favour of claimants.

6. On the point of compensation, it needs to be noted that the accident resulted into death of a person and therefore, the compensation has to be given on the settled principles for calculation.
7.

In the instant case, petition was filed by Ombir Panchal, husband of deceased Maya Devi but later on he expired on 17.07.2018 and thereafter, her daughters and sons namely Meena Devi, Veer Singh, Sonveer, Rachna and Dimpal Sharma remained as LRs/dependant of deceased.
Record reveals that deceased was housewife and all the LRs were major at the time of accident.

Therefore,
they cannot be treated as dependants of deceased Maya Devi who was housewife.
Therefore, there cannot be any loss of dependency.
8. So far as, loss of consortium is concerned fixed sum of Rs.2,42,000/- is awarded.

Besides this,
fixed sum on account of loss of estate and funeral expenses are also allowed as Digitally Rs.18,150/-
and Rs.18,150/- respectively.
signed by RAKESH RAKESH KUMAR KUMAR SINGH SINGH

entities.text: RAKESH RAKESH KUMAR KUMAR SINGH SINGH
entities.label: OTHER_PERSON

sentences.text: There is nothing on record to justify withholding interest 17:59:19 +0530 on the award amount.
Therefore, a simple interest @ 7.5 % per annum is allowed on the Award Amount w.e.f. 26.09.2016 till realization.
If any interim compensation was paid the same shall be deducted from the final compensation.
Liability 10.

Respondent no.1 Man Singh (driver) being principal tortfeasor driving the vehicle no.
UP-11T-4219 in rash/ negligent manner without proper vigil resulting in accident leading to death is primarily liable.
The Man Singh being owner of the vehicle is vicariously liable.
However, since offending vehicle was insured with the insurance company against third party risk so, Insurance Company (insurer) shall pay the award amount with interest to petitioners.
However, the driver did not have endorsement regarding hazardous goods on the DL and therefore, insurance company is allowed to recover the money from the owner.

The accident resulted into death of deceased Maya Devi.
The police registered an FIR No.623/2016 and investigated the matter.
The legal-heirs of Maya Devi has filed claim petition for the purpose of compensation.
The driver and owner appeared and filed joint reply admitting that the accident took place on 10.08.2016 on NH 58.
In terms of Rule 7 of Delhi Motor Accidents Claims Tribunals Rules 2008, the FIR and charge-sheet have to be accepted for their contents.

The driver/owner have not led any evidence to support the proper driving.
It is clear that accident happened due to rash/ negligent driving of Man Singh.
In the instant case, petition was filed by Ombir Panchal, husband of deceased Maya Devi but later on he expired on 17.07.2018 and thereafter, her daughters and sons namely Meena Devi, Veer Singh, Sonveer, Rachna and Dimpal Sharma remained as LRs/dependant of deceased.
Record reveals that deceased was housewife and all the LRs were major at the time of accident.
Therefore,
they cannot be treated as dependants of deceased Maya Devi who was housewife.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
This claim itself shows that the offending vehicle was present at the spot.
Once, the charge-sheet has found the driver as culprit, a prima-facie presumption can be taken that offending driver was rash/negligent.
If the insurance company was of the view that deceased SINGH was solely negligent, it should have appointed its own investigator to investigate the accident and should have led 17:59:15 +0530 evidence in support of its claim.
The insurance company has done neither.
